column4: dialect-gated per SUBTEST: a registeredBackends test, so it runs one subtest per dialect and mysql and mssql skip in these PostgreSQL-only jobs while postgres RUNS -- two, not three. Measured by NAME rather than by delta, with CLEAT_TEST_MYSQL and CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL unset: go test ./engine/ -run TestAWorkflowResultSurvivesTheColumnOrDoesNot -count=1 -json | grep '"Action":"skip"' reports exactly the /mysql and /mssql arms. The arms have to exist even where they skip, because THE WHOLE SUBJECT IS THAT THE THREE DIALECTS DISAGREE: cleat#1022 is a workflow result coming back with a different VALUE depending on the backend, and the degradation is MySQL's alone -- 18446744073709551616 and 0.12345678901234567 survive PostgreSQL and SQL Server and are rewritten by MySQL's JSON column, which stores an integer as INT64 or UINT64 and falls back to DOUBLE when it fits neither. A postgres-only run cannot observe a MySQL-only defect, and dropping the arms would leave the boundary pinned by nothing, which is the state that let two separate measurements of it stay throwaway probes.

dialect-gated per SUBTEST: same test, same two arms, and the cluster job runs ./engine/... too. Measured by name with only CLEAT_TEST_POSTGRES set. See the test-go/engine line above for why the arms exist: the test's subject is a per-dialect divergence in what the result column preserves, so a single-dialect run is not a smaller version of it -- it is a run that cannot see the thing.
